summary: Configured persistent resilient static routing. Direct primary-transit is preferred; tested failover through VyOS completed in about 1.7 seconds, and direct routing returned automatically after restoration.
actions_performed: Configured node2 10.20.12.2 and node3 10.20.13.2 endpoint addresses.
Installed metric-10 direct routes and metric-100 VyOS fallback routes with fixed endpoint source addresses.
Enabled local primary-link health tracking on both Ubuntu endpoints.
Configured and saved VyOS forwarding between lan-a and lan-b only, with no NAT.
Exercised a one-sided primary-link failure, verified fallback, restored the link, and verified recovery.

evidence.requirement: Persistent preferred and fallback static routing
evidence.summary: Final configuration shows persistent metric-10 primary routes, metric-100 fallback routes, enabled health services, saved VyOS interfaces, and forwarding policy.

evidence.requirement: Failover within 10 seconds and automatic recovery
evidence.summary: Healthy traffic used the direct path. Node2 primary transit was lowered at 14:27:53.902; fallback replies resumed around 14:27:55.564 with TTL 63. After restoration at 14:28:19.248, both endpoints reselected the direct path with TTL 64.

evidence.requirement: Preserve endpoint source addresses without NAT
evidence.summary: Packet captures on both direct and fallback paths show unchanged 10.20.12.2↔10.20.13.2 addresses; VyOS has no source-NAT rule.

evidence.requirement: Keep management outside the routed data plane
evidence.summary: Data lookups use only enp8s0/enp9s0, management remains on enp1s0, and VyOS permits forwarding only between eth1 and eth2 while dropping other forwarded traffic.
